title: Toast: Task-Oriented Multi-dimensional Augmentation for Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Data

problem.claim: Data in large repositories can be selectively acquired for augmentation tailored to downstream tasks.

gap.claim: Existing augmentation methods focus mainly on single-dimensional tabular-data augmentation and are not designed to exploit the spatio-temporal characteristics of trajectory data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large data repositories make selective acquisition of data for task-specific augmentation feasible.
Current augmentation methodologies primarily address single-dimensional augmentation for tabular data.
These methods do not adequately use the spatio-temporal characteristics of trajectory data, leading to suboptimal performance.

source_observation.claim: Augmentation methods designed for single-dimensional tabular data do not fully exploit trajectory data's spatio-temporal characteristics.

interpretation.claim: Data augmentation should account for the structural dimensions and properties specific to the target data modality.

application.claim: When augmenting spatio-temporal trajectories, design augmentation around both spatial and temporal structure.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish whether this principle applies beyond trajectory data or to particular downstream tasks.

unknowns: The proposed augmentation method and its implementation are not described.
No downstream tasks, datasets, experiments, quantitative results, or comparisons are supplied.
The claimed source of suboptimal performance is not empirically quantified.
